title: Study Abroad Deposit
text:
Subject: Your Summer in Lisbon deposit

Hi Arjun,

We received your $400 program deposit on March 3. Here is how it applies:

• If you withdraw before April 1, $300 will be refunded; the other $100 is nonrefundable.
• Withdrawals on or after April 1 forfeit the entire deposit.
• Exception: if your student visa is denied, the full $400 is refunded at any time, provided you send us the denial letter within 10 days of receiving it.

Your deposit will be credited toward the $3,200 program fee, and the balance is due May 15. Recipients of the Global Travel Grant may defer the balance until the grant is paid out, but they must notify our office by May 1.

Best regards,
Office of International Programs

questions.prompt: Arjun's visa is denied on March 28. He withdraws from the program on April 4 and sends the denial letter on April 6. How much of his deposit will be refunded?
options: Nothing
questions.explanation: The visa exception refunds the full $400 "at any time" if the denial letter arrives within 10 days; March 28 to April 6 is 9 days, so the April 1 forfeiture rule does not apply.

questions.prompt: The word "defer" in the email is closest in meaning to
options: postpone
reduce
transfer
cancel
questions.explanation: Grant recipients may defer the balance "until the grant is paid out," meaning they may pay it later.

title: Splitting October Utilities
text:
From: Dana Ruiz
To: Leo Park, Mina Cho
Subject: October utilities

Hi both, the October bill is $186: electricity $96 and internet $90. Mina moved in on October 16, so I suggest we prorate only her electricity share; she should pay half of a normal one-third share. Internet is a flat monthly rate we'd pay no matter who lives here, so we split that equally.

From: Leo Park
Fair enough, but I was away October 1–20 and barely used any power. Shouldn't I get the same reduction?

From: Dana Ruiz
Leo, your space heater was on a timer the whole time you were gone, so you'll split the rest with me evenly. Mina, please send your share by November 10. After that, the landlord adds a $15 late fee, which all three of us would have to split.

questions.prompt: How much should Mina pay for October?
questions.explanation: Mina pays an equal third of the internet ($90 ÷ 3 = $30) plus half of a normal electricity third (½ × $96 ÷ 3 = $16), so $30 + $16 = $46.

questions.prompt: What can be inferred about Dana's reply to Leo?
options: She agrees to lower Leo's share of the internet instead.
She thinks Leo should pay less than Mina for electricity.
She expects Leo to pay any late fee by himself.
She believes Leo's room used power while he was away.
questions.explanation: Dana points out that Leo's heater ran on a timer the whole time, so she rejects his request for a reduced electricity share.

questions.prompt: Why does Dana mention the landlord's $15 late fee?
options: To explain why the October bill is higher than usual
To ask Leo to cover the fee because he was away
To show that the October bill has already been paid late
To stress that a late payment by Mina would cost everyone
questions.explanation: Dana says the fee would be added after November 10 and that "all three of us would have to split" it, encouraging Mina to pay on time.

title: Harbor View Moving Reservations
text:
HARBOR VIEW APARTMENTS
Moving Reservations — Summer Update

The freight elevator will be modernized from June 2 to June 13. During this period, moves are allowed only on Saturdays and Sundays, using the passenger elevator with protective padding.

How to reserve
• Book through the resident portal at least 72 hours in advance.
• Weekday slots (after June 13): 9 AM–5 PM, 3-hour limit.
• Weekend slots: 4-hour limit and a $50 deposit, returned if the hallways are left undamaged.

Residents who move without a reservation will be charged $200. This charge is waived for moves involving fewer than five boxes and no furniture.

Questions? Visit the management office in Room 101.

questions.prompt: A resident wants to move a sofa and 20 boxes on Wednesday, June 11. What is true?
options: She may book a 3-hour slot from 9 AM to 5 PM.
She may move without booking if she pays $200.
She must pay a $50 deposit for the weekday slot.
The move cannot take place on that day.
questions.explanation: June 11 falls within the June 2–13 modernization, when moves are allowed only on Saturdays and Sundays; weekday slots begin after June 13.

questions.prompt: The word "waived" in the notice is closest in meaning to
options: increased
delayed
not applied
divided
questions.explanation: The $200 charge is waived for very small moves, meaning those residents are not charged it.

questions.prompt: What can be inferred about the $50 weekend payment?
options: It replaces the $200 charge for moves without a reservation.
A resident who causes no hallway damage will get it back.
It is required only while the freight elevator is closed.
It pays for the padding placed in the passenger elevator.
questions.explanation: The $50 is a deposit "returned if the hallways are left undamaged," so a careful mover ultimately pays nothing for it.

title: Equipment Loan Policy
text:
Media Library — Equipment Loan Policy

Loan periods
• Laptops: 3 days; one renewal allowed if no one is waiting
• Cameras and tripods: 7 days; no renewals

Late fines
• Laptops: $5 per day; cameras: $10 per day; tripods: $2 per day
• Fines begin the day after the due date and stop accruing once they reach the item's replacement cost, which is then billed to the student account.
• Fines are cut in half if the item is returned within 48 hours of the due time and the borrower has no other late returns this semester.

Borrowing privileges are suspended while any fine over $25 remains unpaid. Equipment cannot be returned through the book drop; check it in at the service desk.

questions.prompt: Kenji's camera was due at noon on Monday. He checked it in at the service desk at 10 AM on Wednesday. It was his first late return this semester. How much does he owe?
questions.explanation: Fines run for Tuesday and Wednesday at $10 a day ($20), and because he returned it within 48 hours of the noon Monday due time with no other late returns, the fine is halved to $10.

questions.prompt: According to the policy, which of the following is NOT true of laptops?
options: They can be renewed once if no one is waiting.
They are fined $5 for each day they are late.
They are lent out for three days at a time.
They may be returned through the book drop.
questions.explanation: The policy says equipment "cannot be returned through the book drop"; the other statements are all listed for laptops.

questions.prompt: The word "accruing" in the policy is closest in meaning to
options: being forgiven
accumulating
being reported
being divided
questions.explanation: Fines "stop accruing" at the replacement cost, meaning they stop adding up once they reach that amount.

title: Route 14 Holiday Service
text:

Thu, Nov 27 (Thanksgiving): Sunday schedule (every 40 min, 8 AM–8 PM)

title: Tuition Payment Plan
text:
Spring Tuition Payment Plan — Enrollment Instructions

1. Log in to Student Accounts and select "Payment Plan" between December 1 and January 10.
2. Choose four monthly installments (January–April) or three (February–April). The three-installment option is available only to students who enroll after January 5.
3. Pay the $40 enrollment fee at sign-up. The fee is waived for students receiving need-based aid.
4. Installments are drafted automatically on the 15th of each month. A failed payment results in a $30 charge and must be resolved within 7 days; otherwise, the plan is canceled and the entire remaining balance is due immediately.

Note: All financial aid is applied first, and only the remaining balance is divided into installments.

questions.prompt: Ines owes $5,200 in tuition and has a $1,200 merit scholarship. She enrolls in the plan on December 12. How much will each installment be?
questions.explanation: Aid is applied first ($5,200 − $1,200 = $4,000), and because she enrolled before January 5 she must use four installments: $4,000 ÷ 4 = $1,000.

questions.prompt: What can be concluded about a student whose February payment fails and who resolves it 10 days later?
options: The student will have to pay the $40 enrollment fee again.
The student may switch to the three-installment option.
The student will owe only the $30 failed-payment charge.
The student can no longer pay the balance in installments.
questions.explanation: A failed payment must be resolved within 7 days; after 10 days the plan is canceled and the whole remaining balance is due at once.

questions.prompt: Why do the instructions mention January 5?
options: To set the final day to enroll in the plan
To show when the first payment is drafted
To identify who may choose the shorter plan
To indicate when fee waivers are approved
questions.explanation: Step 2 says the three-installment option is available only to students who enroll after January 5; the enrollment deadline is January 10.

title: Amphitheater Refund Policy
text:
Riverfront Amphitheater — Refunds & Exchanges

All ticket sales are final, except as described below.

Rescheduled shows: Tickets are automatically valid for the new date. If you cannot attend, request a refund within 14 days of the announcement.
Canceled shows: Refunds go automatically to the original payment method within 10 business days.
Weather: Shows go on rain or shine. If a show is stopped after the headliner has performed for 45 minutes, it counts as complete and is not refunded.
Exchanges: Riverfront Club members may exchange tickets for another show this season, up to 48 hours before the original show, for $6 per ticket.

Service fees are not refundable under any circumstances.

questions.prompt: According to the web page, who receives a refund without having to ask for one?
options: People holding tickets to a show that is canceled
People holding tickets to a show that is rescheduled
People at a show stopped after 45 minutes of the headliner
Club members who exchange tickets 48 hours in advance
questions.explanation: Only refunds for canceled shows "go automatically" to the payment method; rescheduled-show refunds must be requested within 14 days.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the web page?
options: To announce that an upcoming show has been moved to a new date
To explain when tickets can be refunded or exchanged
To encourage visitors to become members of the Riverfront Club
To describe the safety procedures followed during bad weather
questions.explanation: The page begins "All ticket sales are final, except as described below" and then lists the exceptions for refunds and exchanges.

title: Lease Early Termination Clause
text:
Lease Agreement — Section 12: Early Termination

12.1 Tenant may end this lease before July 31 by giving 60 days' written notice and paying a termination fee equal to one month's rent ($1,450).
12.2 The fee is reduced by half if Tenant finds a replacement approved by Landlord who begins a new lease within 30 days after Tenant's move-out date.
12.3 Tenant remains responsible for rent until the move-out date stated in the notice or the replacement's lease start date, whichever is earlier.
12.4 Notice given by text message or phone call is not valid.
12.5 Tenants called to active military service may terminate with 30 days' notice and no fee.

questions.prompt: On February 1, Hana delivers a signed letter stating that she will move out on April 1. Her approved replacement signs a lease beginning April 20. What fee will Hana pay?
questions.explanation: Her written notice gives the required 60 days, and the replacement starts 19 days after her move-out date, within 30 days, so the $1,450 fee is halved to $725 (12.2).

questions.prompt: What can be inferred from section 12.3?
options: A tenant must pay rent until July 31 in every case.
A replacement tenant must pay the original tenant's fee.
Rent may end before the move-out date in the notice.
Rent stops on the day the tenant delivers notice.
questions.explanation: Rent is owed until the stated move-out date or the replacement's start date, "whichever is earlier," so a replacement who starts sooner ends the tenant's rent early.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT required of a tenant who ends the lease early because of active military service?
options: Giving at least 30 days' notice
Paying a termination fee
Giving notice in a valid form
Paying rent until the move-out date
questions.explanation: Section 12.5 allows such tenants to terminate "with 30 days' notice and no fee"; the notice and rent rules in 12.3 and 12.4 still apply.

title: Climbing Gym Membership
text:
Summit Climbing Gym — Membership Terms

Monthly rate: $78, billed on the 1st of each month.
Initiation fee: $50. Waived for students with valid ID and for anyone joining in a promotional month (January or September).
First month: Members who join after the 1st pay a prorated amount based on the number of days remaining in that month.
Freezes: $10 per month, for 1–3 months. Requests made before the 25th take effect the following month.
Cancellation: 30 days' written notice is required; the final month is charged in full.
Guests: One guest per member visit. Guest passes cost $18, or half price on Tuesdays.

questions.prompt: Luis, who is not a student, joins in April on a day when exactly half of the month remains. How much does he pay when he signs up?
questions.explanation: His first month is prorated to half of $78 ($39), and because April is not a promotional month and he is not a student, he also pays the $50 initiation fee: $39 + $50 = $89.

questions.prompt: The word "prorated" in the terms is closest in meaning to
options: adjusted to the time covered
charged in full in advance
reduced only for students
split into several payments
questions.explanation: A prorated amount is "based on the number of days remaining," so the charge is proportional to the part of the month used.

title: Delayed Flight Pickup
text:
Maya (2:05 PM): Bad news. My flight's delayed. Now landing at 7:40 instead of 5:15.
Chris (2:07 PM): Ugh. I have class until 7, and campus to the airport is about 50 minutes.
Maya (2:08 PM): No problem, I'll just take the airport shuttle. The last one to campus leaves at 8:30.
Chris (2:10 PM): Customs usually takes about an hour for international arrivals, though.
Maya (2:11 PM): Oh, right. I forgot about that.
Chris (2:12 PM): I'll head out right after class. Text me once you're through customs and I'll meet you at Door 6.
Maya (2:13 PM): Thank you! Dinner's on me.

questions.prompt: Why does Chris write, "Customs usually takes about an hour for international arrivals, though"?
options: To point out that Maya may miss the last shuttle
To explain why Maya's flight has been delayed
To suggest that Maya book a later flight home
To warn that he will arrive after 8:30 PM
questions.explanation: Maya lands at 7:40 and the last shuttle leaves at 8:30; an hour in customs would leave her past 8:30, so Chris is showing that the shuttle plan will not work.

questions.prompt: What can be inferred about Chris's plan?
options: He will reach the airport before Maya's plane lands.
He should reach the airport before Maya clears customs.
He will need to leave his class before it ends.
He will meet Maya at Door 6 at about 5:15.
questions.explanation: Leaving at 7:00 with a 50-minute drive puts Chris there around 7:50, after the 7:40 landing but well before Maya finishes about an hour of customs.

title: Free Tax Help Clinic
text:
FREE TAX HELP — Eastside Community Center
Saturdays, Feb 7 – Apr 11, 10 AM–2 PM (closed Mar 14)

Who qualifies
• Households that earned under $67,000 last year
• International students filing nonresident returns, at any income level (Tuesday evenings only, by appointment)

What to bring
• Photo ID
• Social Security or ITIN cards for everyone listed on the return
• All income forms (W-2, 1099)
• Last year's return, if available

Walk-ins are served in order of arrival; please arrive by 1 PM. Returns that cannot be finished in one visit will be completed by appointment. Volunteers cannot prepare returns that include rental property or more than $10,000 in business income.

questions.prompt: Which person could be helped at the center on a Saturday?
options: An international student filing a nonresident return
A couple whose household earned $72,000 last year
A designer who earned $15,000 in business income
A cashier who earned $41,000 and brings her W-2
questions.explanation: The cashier is under the $67,000 limit; nonresident returns are handled only on Tuesday evenings, $72,000 is over the limit, and business income over $10,000 cannot be prepared.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT something every visitor is required to bring?
options: A form of photo identification
A copy of the previous year's tax return
Income forms such as a W-2 or 1099
A Social Security or ITIN card for each person
questions.explanation: Last year's return is requested only "if available," while the other items are listed without that condition.

title: BIO 210 Late Work Rules
text:
BIO 210 — Late Work and Grading Policies

Lab reports are due Fridays at 11:59 PM. Late reports lose 10% of the earned score for each day late, for up to three days; after that, they receive a zero.

Each student has two grace days per semester. A grace day cancels one day of lateness and may be used on any lab report, but not on the final project.

The lowest quiz score is dropped. A missed quiz counts as zero unless you have a documented medical excuse; an excused quiz is removed from your average and does not count as your dropped score.

Regrade requests must be submitted within one week of grades being posted.

questions.prompt: Priya's lab report earns 80 points, but she submits it two days late and uses one grace day. What is her final score?
questions.explanation: The grace day cancels one of the two late days, leaving one day at a 10% penalty on the earned score: 80 − 8 = 72.

questions.prompt: What can be inferred from the policy?
options: Grace days can be used to reduce the late penalty on the final project.
Unused grace days are converted into extra points on quiz scores.
A report over three days late may still earn some credit.
A student can use a grace day to excuse a quiz that was missed.
questions.explanation: A report five days late becomes three days late after two grace days are applied, which is still within the three-day window, so it earns partial credit instead of a zero.

questions.prompt: Why does the syllabus mention the final project?
options: To announce the date when the final project is due
To explain that it counts as much as two lab reports
To show that its grade may not be submitted for regrading
To name an assignment that grace days cannot be used for
questions.explanation: The final project appears only in the grace-day rule: grace days "may be used on any lab report, but not on the final project."

title: Wireless Headphones Warranty
text:
AeroSound X2 Wireless Headphones — Limited Warranty

Coverage: Defects in materials and workmanship for 1 year from the date of purchase. Batteries are covered for 6 months.
Extended coverage: Register your product online within 30 days of purchase to extend coverage to 2 years (batteries excluded).
Not covered: Damage from drops, water, or unauthorized repairs; cosmetic wear; ear cushions.

Proof of purchase is required for all claims.

options: It will come with a new one-year warranty.
Its battery will be covered for six months.
It must be registered again within 30 days.
It will be covered for about six more months.
questions.explanation: Registration extends coverage to 2 years, and a replacement is covered only for the remainder of the original period, so 24 − 18 leaves about six months.

questions.prompt: The phrase "at our option" in the warranty is closest in meaning to
options: as the customer prefers
for an additional charge
only one time per product
as the company chooses
questions.explanation: "We will repair or replace your product at our option" means the company decides which of the two remedies to provide.

title: Bulk Item Collection Rules
text:
CITY OF FAIRMONT — Bulk Item Collection

Bulk items (furniture, mattresses, appliances) are collected on the first Wednesday of each month. Place items at the curb no earlier than 6 PM on the Monday before and no later than 6 AM on collection day.

• Each household may set out 3 items per month free of charge. Additional items cost $15 each and must be prepaid online.
• Mattresses must be wrapped in plastic, or they will be left behind.
• Refrigerators and air conditioners do not count toward the 3-item limit, but each requires a $25 refrigerant-removal sticker.
• Items set out too early may result in a $75 fine.

If collection day falls on a holiday, pickup moves to Thursday.

questions.prompt: A household sets out a sofa, a wrapped mattress, a table, two chairs, and a refrigerator. How much must it pay?
questions.explanation: The refrigerator does not count toward the limit, so five items count: two extra items at $15 ($30) plus the $25 refrigerator sticker equals $55.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT stated in the notice?
options: Items beyond the monthly limit must be paid for in advance.
Items set out after 6 AM on collection day are fined $75.
Mattresses that are not wrapped in plastic will not be taken.
Pickup moves to Thursday when Wednesday is a holiday.
questions.explanation: The $75 fine applies to items set out too early, not to items placed out late; the other statements appear in the notice.

title: Overnight Guest Policy
text:
Residence Life — Overnight Guest Policy

• Residents may host an overnight guest for up to 3 nights in a row and no more than 6 nights in any calendar month.
• All roommates must agree to each overnight guest. A roommate's objection overrides any earlier agreement.
• Guests must be registered at the front desk by 10 PM on their first night.
• Guests under 17 are not permitted unless they are a resident's sibling and a parent has signed a consent form.
• No overnight guests are allowed in any hall during final exam week.
• Residents are responsible for their guests' behavior and for any damage that guests cause.

questions.prompt: The word "overrides" in the policy is closest in meaning to
options: is added to
takes priority over
is recorded with
is the same as
questions.explanation: A roommate's objection overrides an earlier agreement, meaning the objection counts more than that agreement.

questions.prompt: Emma's friend stayed with her on November 2 and 3. Emma now wants her 15-year-old cousin to stay November 20–22, and her aunt has signed a consent form. Her roommate agrees. Is the visit allowed?
options: No, because it would go over the six-night monthly limit
Yes, because a parent has signed a consent form
Yes, because Emma's roommate has agreed to it
No, because of the guest's age and relationship to Emma
questions.explanation: Guests under 17 are allowed only if they are a resident's sibling with parental consent; a cousin does not qualify, while 2 + 3 = 5 nights would be within the monthly limit.

title: Club Travel Reimbursement
text:
Student Organization Travel Reimbursement — How to Submit

1. Submit Form TR-2 within 30 days of returning from the trip. Late forms will not be processed.
2. Attach itemized receipts. Credit card statements are not accepted as receipts.
3. Personal vehicles are reimbursed at $0.50 per mile. Fuel receipts are not needed, and fuel is not reimbursed separately.
4. Meals are covered up to $40 per traveler per day. Alcohol is never reimbursed.
5. Hotels are covered only if the event is more than 100 miles from campus.
6. Forms must be signed by the organization's treasurer. If the treasurer is the person requesting reimbursement, the faculty advisor signs instead.

Allow 3–4 weeks for payment.

questions.prompt: Jae drove his own car to a conference 90 miles from campus and back. He spent $35 on gas, $120 on one hotel night, and $52 on meals over two days, never more than $40 in one day. How much will be reimbursed?
questions.explanation: He receives 180 miles × $0.50 = $90 plus $52 for meals; gas is not reimbursed separately, and the hotel is not covered because the event is less than 100 miles away: $90 + $52 = $142.

questions.prompt: According to the instructions, which expense is NOT reimbursable under any circumstances?
options: Alcoholic drinks ordered with a meal
A hotel room for an overnight event
A meal costing less than $40 a day
Mileage driven in a personal vehicle

title: Coworking Passes and Rooms
text:

Day Pass: $25 (8 AM–6 PM). Includes Wi-Fi, coffee, and 30 minutes of free meeting room time.
10-Day Bundle: $200, valid for 90 days from first use. Unused days expire and are not refunded.
Monthly Membership: $280. The only option that includes evening access (6–10 PM).
Meeting Rooms: $15 per hour for pass holders and members; $30 per hour for everyone else. Rooms are booked in 30-minute increments.

Changes: Meeting rooms canceled at least 24 hours in advance are free. Later cancellations are billed in full unless another customer books the same time.

questions.prompt: Grace buys a Day Pass and books a meeting room for two hours. What is her total cost?
questions.explanation: The Day Pass includes 30 free minutes, so she pays for 1.5 hours at the pass-holder rate: $25 + (1.5 × $15 = $22.50) = $47.50.

questions.prompt: What can be inferred about the 10-Day Bundle?

It includes access to the space after 6 PM.

questions.prompt: The word "increments" in the web page is closest in meaning to

deposits
shifts
units
questions.explanation: Rooms are "booked in 30-minute increments," meaning in blocks or units of 30 minutes.

title: Car Sharing Member Terms
text:
GoShare Car Sharing — Member Terms (Excerpt)

Rates: $11 per hour or $79 per day (24 hours), whichever is lower. Gas and insurance are included.
Mileage: The first 180 miles of each reservation are free; each additional mile costs $0.45.
Late returns: $50 fee plus the hourly rate for the extra time. If your lateness delays the next member's reservation, the fee rises to $75.
Fuel: Return the car with at least a quarter tank. Use the fuel card in the glove box; if you pay with your own money, you will be reimbursed when you upload the receipt within 7 days.
Damage: Report any damage before starting your trip.

questions.prompt: Ana reserves a car for 9 hours, drives 220 miles, and returns it on time. What does she pay?

title: Farewell Gift Group Chat
text:

Ravi: Could I pay you Tuesday instead? I get paid that day.
Nora: Sure. And I'll buy the card myself, so don't worry about that.
Sam: Thanks, Nora!

questions.prompt: How much will Sam pay?
questions.explanation: The pen costs $96 × 0.85 = $81.60, plus $12 engraving is $93.60; after Jo's $10, the remaining $83.60 is split among five people: $16.72 each.

questions.prompt: What can be inferred about the discount Kai mentions?
options: It will lower the cost of the engraving as well.
The group will get it because of when Nora orders.
It requires everyone to pay Nora by Friday.
It will be used to pay for the card.
questions.explanation: The discount applies to orders placed by Friday, and Nora says she will order on Thursday, so the group qualifies.

questions.prompt: Why does Ravi write, "I get paid that day"?
options: To offer to cover Jo's share of the gift
To suggest that the order wait until Tuesday
To say that he will pay for the card
To explain why he cannot pay by Nora's date
questions.explanation: Nora asks for shares by Monday; Ravi asks to pay Tuesday and gives his payday as the reason.

title: CHEM 101 Lab Attendance
text:
CHEM 101 Lab — Attendance and Make-Up Policy

There are 10 weekly labs, and your lowest lab score is dropped.
• Safety goggles and closed-toe shoes are required. Students who arrive without them will be sent home, and the absence will count as unexcused.
• Unexcused absences receive a zero. A second unexcused absence results in failing the lab component, regardless of other scores.
• Excused absences (documented illness or university-sponsored travel) may be made up only during Make-Up Week (Week 14). No more than two labs may be made up.
• Students arriving more than 15 minutes late may not begin the experiment.

questions.prompt: Ines was sent home in Week 3 for wearing sandals, and in Week 9 she missed lab because she overslept. What will happen?
options: She will make up the Week 9 lab in Week 14.
Her Week 3 zero will be dropped with no other effect.
She will fail the lab part of the course.
She may make up both labs during Make-Up Week.
questions.explanation: Being sent home for improper shoes counts as unexcused, and oversleeping is also unexcused; a second unexcused absence means failing the lab component regardless of other scores.

questions.prompt: Why does the policy mention university-sponsored travel?
options: To explain why Make-Up Week is scheduled in Week 14
To give an example of an absence that can be made up
To list a reason students may arrive late to lab
To describe a field trip that every student takes
questions.explanation: University-sponsored travel appears in parentheses as one type of excused absence, which may be made up during Week 14.

title: Refurbished Espresso Machine Warranty
text:

Your refurbished espresso machine is covered against defects for 180 days from delivery.
• Descale the machine every 3 months as described in the manual. Failure to do so voids this warranty for pump-related claims only.
• Damage caused by using unfiltered hard water is not covered.
• Covered machines will be repaired. If a repair is not possible, you will receive store credit for the purchase price, not a cash refund.
• Care Plan: If purchased within 60 days of delivery, it extends coverage to 2 years and provides a replacement machine, rather than a repair, for covered defects.
• Claims require your order number; the original box is not needed.

title: Self Storage Rental Terms
text:
SecureSpace Self Storage — Rental Terms

Rent is due on the 1st of each month. A $20 late fee is added on the 6th.
If rent is unpaid for 30 days, access to the unit is suspended and a company lock is added. After 60 days unpaid, contents may be sold at auction; proceeds first cover unpaid rent and fees, and any remainder is mailed to the renter.
Move-out: Give notice by the 20th to avoid being charged for the following month. Partial months are not prorated.
First-month special: 50% off the first month's rent, for 10×10 units only. The $25 administrative fee is nonrefundable.
Insurance is required. Renters may use their own policy or buy ours for $12 per month.

title: Replacing a Campus ID Card
text:
Campus Card Office — Replacing Your ID Card

Lost or stolen cards: Deactivate your card right away in the CampusCard app. The replacement fee is $25, but it is waived if you report the card stolen and provide a police report number.
Damaged cards: Bring the damaged card to our office for a free replacement. However, cards damaged by punching holes, bending, or adding stickers are charged the full $25.
Name changes: Free, once the Registrar has updated your record.

Meal swipes and printing funds move to the new card automatically. Building access can take up to 24 hours to update, so on-campus residents receive a temporary access pass.

Office hours: Mon–Fri, 9 AM–4:30 PM. After hours, call Campus Safety for a temporary pass.
